images.caption: Figure 2:Overview of the Reforge dataset. Execution variations span translation, rotation, and closure timing; observed consequences include failed contact, object responses, and grasp outcomes. Consecutive RGB frames illustrate representative changes. Top counts cover the full dataset; bars summarize simulated trajectories, with overlapping output labels.

Figure 3:WorldReforge augments an action-conditioned DiT with spatial and temporal supervision. The initial observation and future actions condition flow-matching prediction. Interaction Alignment weights reconstruction in interaction regions; Surface Correspondence uses physical GT to align the same surface points across frames through backbone features. RGB examples illustrate regions and tracks. Both auxiliary objectives share the backbone without adding inference-time parameters.

Figure 4:Different actions produce different physical responses: the marker slips in execution A and is lifted in B. Top: shared Frame 0 and recorded Frame 16 outcomes. Bottom: wrist-view RMS maps of the RGB branch-difference residual over all future frames and channels; darker indicates lower error. RDE for this pair’s wrist view is displayed×103\times 10^{3}.
Fig. S1:Reforge-Real capture setup and three-view observations. The right panel shows the wrist and two external views from the same recorded interaction with a marker.

Fig. S3:Long interaction sequences from Reforge, DROID, and Reforge-Real. Simulated examples show, in order, a bagel, milk carton, spring clamp, mustard bottle, red pepper, and remote control; DROID shows a book and a block; Reforge-Real shows a plush toy and a mango. Each row spans approximately 4.3 seconds at seven timestamps. Each frame retains the full wrist view above the two external views.

Fig. S4:Three-view predictions of simulated interactions. The upper two examples show a sauce bottle and marker seen during post-training; the lower two show an unseen Rubik’s cube and red mug. Each example presents GT, Pretrained, and WorldReforge, with seven columns spanning frames 0–16. WorldReforge more accurately reproduces the displacement and rotation of these objects.

Fig. S5:Three-view predictions of real-world interactions. The upper two examples show a funnel and orange from DROID; the lower two show contact-induced strawberry displacement and beverage-bottle rotation from Reforge-Real. Each example presents GT, Pretrained, and WorldReforge over seven columns spanning frames 0–16. WorldReforge better follows these objects’ changes in position and orientation.
